verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED (not refuted), but severity is MINOR. I re-derived everything from artifacts.

ARITHMETIC (run_a0_restricted*.json, run_a3_n45*.json, run_a3_n8.json): A0 mean=1303.2, A3@N45=1252.0, A3@N8=1119.4, r=A0/A1=1303.2/645.6=2.019. Reviewer's per-check pp: 1.715/4=0.429 vs 2.809/23=0.122 pp/check = 3.51x, opposite direction — confirmed.

The pp/check metric is crude, so I re-tested in the physically-correct absolute-time frame. Backing out the implied FIXED per-check D2H cost c (using A1's measured checked-step compute 1/645.6 and A0's vanilla step time 1/1303.2): c@N45=630.5 us-units vs c@N8=226.4 us-units = 2.79x, larger at N45 (FEWER checks). So the non-constancy survives the rigorous framing — the reviewer's observation is not an artifact of the crude pp metric.

The shim (rv_coop_shim.c:175) does ONE fixed-size 256-byte (slots_used*2=128*2) legacy-stream cudaMemcpy D2H per check, identical for both N (coop_driver.py:99 rv_read once per checked step). CONFIRMED material, not refuted. I re-derived the mechanism from source and logs rather than taking the reviewer's word.

MECHANISM (confirmed by source): For A3, coop_driver.py:62 calls rv_arm(1 if ARM=='a2' else 0, 1 if ARM=='a1' else 0) = rv_arm(0,0) before the vanilla _orig_call (line 63). The shim rv_arm (rv_coop_shim.c:153) sets f_log=0, f_checks=0, cap_lin=0. Contrast A1: line 62 sets f_checks=1 during _orig_call, so A1's inject IS in vLLM's single, every-step-replayed graph (genuinely persistent).

CONSEQUENCE (confirmed): In A3's replay path (coop_driver.py:93-111), the checked graph (containing BOTH inject and inline check) is replayed only every Nth step; all other steps replay the vanilla graph, which has NEITHER inject NOR check. So the fault physically exists only on the checked steps and is inseparably co-located with the check — the check examines a graph that contains the fault and cannot miss it. This is the easiest possible detection condition, NOT a persistent fault present on every step that a periodic check samples at the next check (the ≤N-1 latency case). A1 (non-shippable, single graph) genuinely tests the persistent case; A3 (the shippable -3.9% dual-graph design) does not.

1. Factual error in the artifacts: Report L27-28 'flips bit-14 of C[0]... every replay (persistent SDC)', PREREG L18 'persistent, fires every replay', and driver comment coop_driver.py:59 'inject is armed for ALL captures (persistent fault fires on every replay of either graph)' are all FALSE for A3 — the vanilla graph (replayed 41/45 @N45, 7/8 @N8) is clean and the inject lives only in the checked graph.
2. CONSEQUENCE (confirmed): In A3's replay path (coop_driver.py:93-111), the checked graph (containing BOTH inject and inline check) is replayed only every Nth step; all other steps replay the vanilla graph, which has NEITHER inject NOR check. So the fault physically exists only on the checked steps and is inseparably co-located with the check — the check examines a graph that contains the fault and cannot miss it. This is the easiest possible detection condition, NOT a persistent fault present on every step that a periodic check samples at the next check (the ≤N-1 latency case). A1 (non-shippable, single graph) genuinely tests the persistent case; A3 (the shippable -3.9% dual-graph design) does not.

WHY MATERIAL:
1. Factual error in the artifacts: Report L27-28 'flips bit-14 of C[0]... every replay (persistent SDC)', PREREG L18 'persistent, fires every replay', and driver comment coop_driver.py:59 'inject is armed for ALL captures (persistent fault fires on every replay of either graph)' are all FALSE for A3 — the vanilla graph (replayed 41/45 @N45, 7/8 @N8) is clean and the inject lives only in the checked graph.
2. Overclaimed verdict / undisclosed methodology gap: The report headline (L5 'catch-at-first-check ≤ N', L104 'persistent-within-N') and PREREG pred 4 ('persistent flip caught at FIRST checked step, latency ≤N-1') claim the periodic-sampling detection-latency property is validated for the dual-graph design. The A3 inject run does NOT test this — it tests only the co-located case. The ≤N-1 latency property is genuinely untested for the shippable A3 design, and the report nowhere discloses that the A3 vanilla graph is clean / fault lives only in the checked graph.

The cost numbers (-3.9%/-14.1%), 0-FP (clean runs), and the capture-time-survives mechanism finding are unaffected — but the detection-validity claim for the shippable design is overstated and the injection framing is factually wrong for A3.

Not refuted; not downgradeable to minor because a decision-maker would wrongly conclude the dual-graph design's periodic-sampling detection latency was demonstrated when it was not. The reviewer's suggested fixes (disclose A3 vanilla-clean/checked-only inject and relabel as 'check-co-located fault caught at checked step', or re-run with inject also armed into the vanilla graph; fix the misleading driver:59 comment) are appropriate.

finding.title: The analytic-vs-measured throughput gap is attributed to a D2H sync stall 'scaling with checked steps', but the per-check gap moves the opposite way and no run isolates the cause
finding.report_claim: Report L80-85: 'Analytic dual-graph marginal ... predicts −2.2% @N45, −11.3% @N8. Measured −3.9% / −14.1% — higher by 1.7 pp / 2.8 pp, the gap scaling with the number of checked steps (4 @N45, 23 @N8). The excess is the legacy-stream cudaMemcpy D2H readback that syncs the device once per checked step.'
finding.evidence: Recomputed: Amdahl N/((N-1)+r) with r=A0/A1=1303.2/645.6=2.019 gives −2.21%@N45 and −11.29%@N8 (matches). But the gap PER CHECKED STEP is N45: 1.7pp/4 = 0.43pp/check vs N8: 2.8pp/23 = 0.12pp/check — a 3.5x difference in the WRONG direction for a fixed per-check D2H stall (a constant per-checked-step cost would give roughly equal pp/check, with the larger total at N8 simply from more checks). The data are inconsistent with the stated 'once per checked step' fixed-cost mechanism. No run isolates this: grep of all JSON/logs finds no deferred-read / no-readback / async variant; rv_read (rv_coop_shim.c:172-180) always does a synchronous legacy-stream cudaMemcpy D2H, and there is no control run removing it. The 'D2H readback explains the excess' is asserted, not measured.
finding.suggested_fix: Either run an isolating variant (A3 with the D2H read removed or made async, or a checked-step that replays g_chk but skips rv_read) to quantify the readback's contribution, or downgrade the claim to 'the excess is consistent with per-checked-step overheads including the D2H readback and python-side replay dispatch; not isolated.' Drop the 'gap scaling with the number of checked steps' phrasing, which the per-check arithmetic (0.43 vs 0.12 pp/check) contradicts.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced every number from the artifacts. From the run JSONs: A0=(1302.8+1303.6)/2=1303.2, A1=645.6 (run_a1_n45.json), A3_n45=(1252.0+1251.4)/2=1251.7, A3_n8=1119.4 (run_a3_n8.json). r=A0/A1=2.019 (matches report's 2.02). Amdahl N/((N-1)+r): -2.21%@N45, -11.29%@N8 (matches report's -2.2/-11.3). Measured deltas vs A0: -3.95%@N45, -14.10%@N8 (matches report's -3.9/-14.1). Excess gaps 1.74pp/2.81pp (matches report's 1.7/2.8). Checked steps 4@N45, 23@N8, confirmed via shim_stats.reads==checks in every JSON.

The mechanism claim is contradicted by the report's own data. Per-checked-step gap = 0.43pp/check @N45 vs 0.12pp/check @N8 — a 3.56x difference in the WRONG direction for a fixed once-per-check D2H cost. Modeling a fixed per-check stall c in normal-step-time units (ratio = N/((N-1)+r+c)) yields c=0.83@N45 vs c=0.295@N8 — 2.82x apart, when a genuinely fixed cost requires them equal. A fixed per-check cost would make the N8 gap ~5.75x the N45 gap (since N8 has 5.75x more checks, 23 vs 4); measured ratio is only 1.62x. So a fixed D2H readback OVER-predicts the N8 gap by ~3.5x and cannot reconcile both points.

The shim (rv_coop_shim.c:172-180, rv_read) always does a synchronous legacy-stream cudaMemcpy D2H, called exactly once per checked step (coop_driver.py:99). Grep across all .py/.c/.log/.json finds NO async/deferred/device-pointer/no-readback variant and NO control arm that removes the readback. So the D2H attribution is asserted, never isolated. PREREG pred 3 only ever MODELED readback as a per-N term; it was never measured independently, yet the report states 'a measured D2H-sync stall' and 'the gap scaling with the number of checked steps... now quantified' (L80-85).

Material: the report presents an unexplained excess overhead as a understood, bounded, recoverable fixed cost (L84-85: 'A device-pointer-mode result kept on-GPU with a deferred async read would recover most of it'). A decision-maker would wrongly conclude the overhead source is known and removable. Both the phrase 'gap scaling with the number of checked steps' (per-check it shrinks 0.43->0.12) and the 'fixed once-per-checked-step D2H' attribution are contradicted by the artifacts. Tried to refute; the reviewer's recomputation reproduces exactly and the steelman (gap merely monotonic in checks) fails because the report explicitly invokes proportional 'scaling' and a fixed per-check mechanism. Minor caveat: location field is 'unspecified' but the cited L80-85 and claim text are accurate, so this does not weaken the finding.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute this finding against the artifacts and could not; every element reproduces exactly.

finding.title: Finding 4's per-checked-step excess pattern contradicts the asserted 'fixed per-check D2H sync' cause, which is stated definitively but never isolated
finding.report_claim: Report Finding 4 (lines 80-85): 'Measured −3.9 % / −14.1 % — higher by 1.7 pp / 2.8 pp, the gap scaling with the number of checked steps (4 @N45, 23 @N8). The excess IS the legacy-stream cudaMemcpy D2H readback that syncs the device once per checked step.'
finding.evidence: If the excess were a fixed-cost D2H sync 'once per checked step,' the excess expressed as pp should be roughly constant per check. It is not: excess 1.716pp over 4 checks = 0.43 pp/check @N45 vs 2.81pp over 23 checks = 0.122 pp/check @N8 — a 3.5x difference, and in the wrong direction (larger per-check excess when there are FEWER checks). The report asserts the cause as established fact ('The excess IS...') but ran no isolating experiment (no run with the readback disabled / device-pointer-mode kept on-GPU — explicitly 'left as a named optimization, not built', line 85). Weak corroboration exists (A2 sidecar −4.1% ≈ A3 full-second-graph −3.9% per checked step despite A2 doing far less compute, run_a2_n45.json vs run_a3_n45.json, consistent with a common fixed per-check cost), but the per-check-excess magnitudes do not support the clean fixed-cost-per-sync story the prose claims.
finding.suggested_fix: Soften from 'The excess IS the D2H readback' to 'consistent with / attributable to' and note it is not isolated. Either drop 'the gap scaling with the number of checked steps' (the per-check excess actually moves opposite to a fixed per-check cost) or add the isolating run (device-pointer deferred-read) that would pin the cause. State plainly that 1.7pp/2.8pp is an unattributed overhead above the Amdahl model whose dominant component is hypothesized, not measured, to be the legacy-stream D2H sync.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED (not refuted), but severity is MINOR. I re-derived everything from artifacts.

ARITHMETIC (run_a0_restricted*.json, run_a3_n45*.json, run_a3_n8.json): A0 mean=1303.2, A3@N45=1252.0, A3@N8=1119.4, r=A0/A1=1303.2/645.6=2.019. Amdahl N/((N-1)+r) predicts -2.21%/-11.29%; measured -3.93%/-14.10%; excess 1.715pp/2.809pp (report rounds 1.7/2.8 — exact). Reviewer's per-check pp: 1.715/4=0.429 vs 2.809/23=0.122 pp/check = 3.51x, opposite direction — confirmed.

The pp/check metric is crude, so I re-tested in the physically-correct absolute-time frame. Backing out the implied FIXED per-check D2H cost c (using A1's measured checked-step compute 1/645.6 and A0's vanilla step time 1/1303.2): c@N45=630.5 us-units vs c@N8=226.4 us-units = 2.79x, larger at N45 (FEWER checks). A genuine fixed per-check cost requires c@N45==c@N8. Total excess grows sublinearly (2.02x excess for 5.75x checks). So the non-constancy survives the rigorous framing — the reviewer's observation is not an artifact of the crude pp metric.

The shim (rv_coop_shim.c:175) does ONE fixed-size 256-byte (slots_used*2=128*2) legacy-stream cudaMemcpy D2H per check, identical for both N (coop_driver.py:99 rv_read once per checked step). So the IMPLEMENTATION is genuinely a fixed per-check cost — which makes the measured 2.79x non-constancy a real unexplained puzzle, directly contradicting the report's flat assertion (line 83) 'The excess IS the legacy-stream cudaMemcpy D2H readback that syncs the device once per checked step' and the sub-clause 'the gap scaling with the number of checked steps' (line 82) — which is offered as evidence FOR a per-check cost but is self-undermining since per-check excess moves opposite. No isolating run exists (line 85: deferred-read 'left as a named optimization, not built'), so the cause is asserted, not measured.

Refutations I tried and rejected: (1) noise — excess is 22.4 tok/s @N45 / 36.6 tok/s @N8 vs <1 tok/s observed run-to-run variance (A0 1302.8/1303.6, A3@N45 1252.0/1251.4); (2) wrong r — A1's checked-step compute is the correct r for A3's checked-graph replay (both replay the same captured checked full graph); (3) per-step python dispatch overhead — would be N-independent in total time, cannot produce the N-dependent excess, and is not the cause the report claims.

SEVERITY = MINOR rather than material: it does NOT touch a headline number (-3.9%/-14.1% are measured directly and repeated for N45) or the verdict (cudagraph-frame hosting marginal, eager tax eliminated). It is a misattribution of a small second-order ~1.7-2.8pp residual within an already-small overhead; the deployment decision and the 'deferred-read could recover some' guidance are unchanged. The defect is in explanatory prose stated as fact, plus one self-undermining sub-clause, not in any load-bearing measurement. The reviewer's suggested fix is correct: soften 'IS' to 'consistent with / attributable to', state it is not isolated, and drop or qualify 'scaling with checked steps'.
